national/agency: Minnesota names FOUR relationships on a statutory disclosure form - SELLER'S BROKER, BUYER'S BROKER, DUAL AGENT and FACILITATOR - due at FIRST SUBSTANTIVE CONTACT in a residential transaction (82.67).
FACILITATOR is the DEFAULT until a representation contract is signed, and a facilitator owes NO fiduciary duty EXCEPT CONFIDENTIALITY (82.67 subd. 3, paragraph IV).
A facilitator who shows their OWN LISTING to their buyer MUST ACT AS A SELLER'S BROKER - the statute converts the role rather than creating dual agency (82.67 subd. 3).
TWO SALESPERSONS OF THE SAME BROKER each representing a party IS dual agency, and residential consent goes in the PURCHASE AGREEMENT in a BOXED statutory format (82.67 subd. 3, subd. 4).
A Minnesota dual agent may NOT ADVOCATE for one party to the detriment of the other; PRICE, TERMS AND MOTIVATION stay confidential and EVERYTHING ELSE IS SHARED (82.67 subd. 3).
Suicide, accidental death, natural death and PERCEIVED PARANORMAL ACTIVITY are NOT MATERIAL FACTS by statute (82.68 subd. 3(b)).
national/disclosures: The SELLER's duty is a GENERAL WRITTEN DISCLOSURE OF MATERIAL FACTS, not a mandated checklist - and it CAN BE WAIVED by written agreement of seller and buyer (513.55, 513.60).
A waiver does NOT reach the WELL (103I.235) or SUBSURFACE SEWAGE (115.55 subd. 6) disclosures, which are separate statutory duties (513.60).

A WELL DISCLOSURE CERTIFICATE is a RECORDING PREREQUISITE: without it, or the statutory no-wells statement on the deed, the recorder may not record a deed requiring a certificate of value (103I.235 subd. 1(h)).
A failure-to-disclose action must be brought WITHIN TWO YEARS OF CLOSING (513.57 subd. 2).
NEWLY CONSTRUCTED, NEVER-INHABITED property and a TRANSFER TO A TENANT IN POSSESSION are among the fourteen exemptions (513.54).

STATUTORY HOME WARRANTIES run ONE YEAR (workmanship and materials), TWO YEARS (plumbing, electrical, heating and cooling installation) and TEN YEARS (major construction defects), and SURVIVE THE PASSAGE OF TITLE (327A.02).

examples: A licensee meets a buyer at an open house and starts discussing what the buyer can afford. What is owed, and when?

The agency disclosure form is due at that first substantive contact. Until the buyer signs a representation contract the buyer is a CUSTOMER, and the licensee is a facilitator unless already representing the seller - in which case the licensee must act in the seller's best interest and tell the seller anything the buyer discloses (82.67).
A facilitator working with a buyer takes them to a house the facilitator listed last month.
The facilitator MUST act as a seller's broker from that point (82.67 subd. 3, paragraph IV). This is not dual agency - the statute converts the role, it does not split it.
Two salespersons at the same brokerage, one with the seller and one with the buyer, put a deal together.

That is dual agency in Minnesota. The broker must make full disclosure to all parties and get consent in the purchase agreement in the statutory boxed wording. Price, terms and motivation stay confidential; everything else is shared (82.67 subd. 3, subd. 4).

BUYER'S BROKER: a buyer may agree that the broker represents and acts on the buyer's behalf. The broker may represent THE BUYER ONLY, AND NOT THE SELLER, EVEN IF PAID IN WHOLE OR IN PART BY THE SELLER.

DUAL AGENT: one broker or salesperson represents BOTH parties, OR TWO SALESPERSONS LICENSED TO THE SAME BROKER each represent a party. It requires the INFORMED CONSENT OF ALL PARTIES, means the SAME DUTIES are owed to both, LIMITS the level of representation, and PROHIBITS acting exclusively for either party. DUAL AGENTS MAY NOT ADVOCATE FOR ONE PARTY TO THE DETRIMENT OF THE OTHER.

In a dual agency, CONFIDENTIAL INFORMATION ABOUT PRICE, TERMS AND MOTIVATION is kept confidential UNLESS the party instructs the broker IN WRITING to disclose specific information about that party. OTHER INFORMATION WILL BE SHARED.

FACILITATOR: a broker or salesperson who performs services for a buyer, a seller or both but REPRESENTS NEITHER in a fiduciary capacity. The statute says in capitals that the facilitator OWES NO PARTY ANY OF THE FIDUCIARY DUTIES EXCEPT CONFIDENTIALITY, unless a WRITTEN FACILITATOR SERVICES AGREEMENT includes them.

mn/agency.summary: Seven items, and the part of Minnesota law most likely to trip up someone who studied another state. Minnesota names FOUR relationships on a statutory form, treats an unrepresented consumer as a CUSTOMER, and makes FACILITATOR the default until a representation contract is signed.
traps: FACILITATOR is the default until a representation contract is signed, and a facilitator owes ONLY CONFIDENTIALITY.
A facilitator who shows their OWN LISTING to their buyer becomes a SELLER'S BROKER, not a dual agent.
Two salespersons of the SAME broker each representing a party is DUAL AGENCY in Minnesota.
Dual agency confidentiality covers PRICE, TERMS AND MOTIVATION; everything else IS SHARED.
Residential dual agency consent goes IN THE PURCHASE AGREEMENT, in a BOXED format.
Suicide, natural death, accidental death and perceived paranormal activity are NOT material facts by statute.
The agency disclosure form is RESIDENTIAL ONLY and is NOT a representation contract.
vocab: Facilitator

A licensee who performs services for a buyer, seller or both without representing either in a fiduciary capacity, owing only confidentiality unless a written facilitator services agreement adds duties (82.67 subd. 3).
Customer
A consumer who has not signed a representation contract, and so receives no representation (82.67 subd. 3).
First substantive contact
The moment the agency disclosure form is due in a residential transaction (82.67 subd. 1).
Material fact
A fact the licensee is aware of that could adversely and significantly affect an ordinary purchaser's use or enjoyment of the property, or an intended use the licensee knows of (82.68 subd. 3(a)).
BPO fee
The fee for a broker price opinion, which a licensee may accept only from their own broker unless authorised in writing (82.70 subd. 1, 82.735).
Protective list
The list a licensee must furnish within 72 hours after a listing or buyer's broker agreement expires in order to enforce an override clause (82.66).

EVERY LISTING AGREEMENT MUST BE IN WRITING and include: a DEFINITE EXPIRATION DATE; a description of the property; the LIST PRICE and any terms the seller requires; the amount of compensation OR THE BASIS FOR COMPUTING IT; a clear statement of the EVENTS OR CONDITIONS entitling the broker to a commission; a clear statement of WHETHER AND HOW THE AGREEMENT MAY BE CANCELLED; the OVERRIDE CLAUSE information if applicable, including that the override clause is INEFFECTIVE UNLESS a PROTECTIVE LIST is supplied WITHIN 72 HOURS after expiration; the TEN-POINT BOLDFACE COMPENSATION NOTICE; for residential, the DUAL AGENCY DISCLOSURE STATEMENT with the seller's written instruction; a notice requiring the seller to STATE IN WRITING whether the licensee may ARRANGE CLOSING SERVICES; and for residential, notice that AFTER EXPIRATION the seller owes no fee if the seller has signed another valid listing obliging payment to a different licensee.

THE BUSINESS-SALE EXCEPTION: a listing used with the PURCHASE OR SALE OF A BUSINESS may carry an override clause OF UP TO TWO YEARS, negotiable with the seller, and the protective list must include each named party's WRITTEN ACKNOWLEDGMENT that the business was presented to them by the licensee (82.66 subd. 1(d)(2)).

l: ALL WRITTEN OFFERS to purchase or lease shall be PROMPTLY SUBMITTED IN WRITING to the seller or lessor (82.71 subd. 1).
A licensee SHALL NOT DISCLOSE THE TERMS OF AN OFFER to another prospective buyer, or to the licensee representing or assisting that buyer, BEFORE THE OFFER IS PRESENTED TO THE SELLER (82.71 subd. 2).

Licensees must disclose to a buyer or seller, AT OR BEFORE the time an offer is WRITTEN OR PRESENTED, that CLOSING COSTS may reduce the seller's proceeds or increase the buyer's cash outlay (82.71 subd. 3).

Licensees must furnish the parties a TRUE AND ACCURATE COPY of listing agreements, earnest money receipts, purchase agreements, contracts for deed, option agreements, closing statements, TRUTH-IN-HOUSING FORMS, ENERGY AUDITS and any other material record in the licensee's possession, AT THE TIME THE DOCUMENTS ARE SIGNED OR BECOME AVAILABLE (82.71 subd. 4).

If the LISTING BROKER acts as the transaction CLOSING AGENT, the broker must deliver AT CLOSING a complete and detailed CLOSING STATEMENT to the seller showing all receipts and disbursements handled for the seller, and a statement to the BUYER showing the disposition of all money received from the buyer (82.71 subd. 5).

RETENTION: a broker must RETAIN FOR SIX YEARS copies of all listings, buyer representation and facilitator services contracts, deposit receipts, purchase money contracts, cancelled checks, trust account records and other documents reasonably related to the business. The period runs FROM THE DATE OF CLOSING, or FROM THE DATE OF THE DOCUMENT if the transaction is not consummated (82.72 subd. 3).

TWO THINGS NEED NOT BE RETAINED: agency disclosure forms where NO CONTRACTUAL RELATIONSHIP followed and no services were provided; and facilitator services or buyer representation contracts where the prospective buyer ABANDONED the relationship before any services were provided.

Storage MAY BE ELECTRONIC (82.72 subd. 4). After the six years, disposal must follow the CONFIDENTIAL RECORD DESTRUCTION procedures of the FAIR AND ACCURATE CREDIT TRANSACTION ACT OF 2003 (82.72 subd. 5). The COMMISSIONER MAY EXAMINE a broker's records WITHIN OR OUTSIDE THE STATE at any reasonable time (82.72 subd. 2).

SUPERVISION: a broker must ADEQUATELY SUPERVISE the activities of the broker's salespersons and employees, including ONGOING MONITORING of listing agreements, purchase agreements and other documents prepared by or received in the office, and REVIEW OF ALL TRUST ACCOUNT BOOKS AND RECORDS. Each place of business must be under the direction and supervision of an individual broker, and DESIGNATING ANOTHER BROKER DOES NOT RELIEVE THE PRIMARY BROKER of ultimate responsibility (82.73 subd. 3(a)).
A broker is responsible for the PREPARATION, CUSTODY, SAFETY AND ACCURACY of all contracts, documents and records EVEN IF ANOTHER PERSON IS ASSIGNED THOSE DUTIES (82.73 subd. 3(b)).

COMPLAINTS: a broker must INVESTIGATE AND ATTEMPT TO RESOLVE complaints about anyone licensed to the broker, and maintain a COMPLAINT FILE for each such individual containing all material on complaints RECEIVED IN WRITING FOR THREE YEARS (82.73 subd. 3(c)).

UNLICENSED STAFF: a broker MAY allow an authorised unlicensed person to disclose FACTUAL INFORMATION about the broker's listings, IF the information is PROVIDED TO THEM IN WRITTEN FORM BY THE BROKER representing or assisting the seller (82.73 subd. 3(d)).
Every real estate office and BRANCH OFFICE must keep a CURRENT COPY of chapter 82, chapter 83 and the rules AVAILABLE FOR LICENSEES' USE - access may be through an ELECTRONIC AGENT (82.73 subd. 1).

Failure to comply with the standards in 82.73 subd. 1 and 3 and sections 82.67, 82.70, 82.71, 82.74 and 82.81 subd. 10 is a ground for LICENCE DENIAL, SUSPENSION OR REVOCATION, OR CENSURE (82.73 subd. 2).

l: NO HOLD HARMLESS OR ARBITRATION CLAUSE addressing the rights or liabilities of persons required to be licensed may appear in a purchase agreement, earnest money contract or similar contract - UNLESS the person required to be licensed is A PRINCIPAL in the transaction. Separate and independent written agreements are not prohibited (82.81 subd. 5). A licensee may not sue to enforce a provision that violates this (82.85 subd. 4).

CLOSING SERVICES: no licensee or closing agent may REQUIRE a person to use ANY PARTICULAR LENDER, LICENSED ATTORNEY, BROKER, SALESPERSON, CLOSING AGENT OR TITLE INSURANCE AGENT in connection with a RESIDENTIAL closing (82.81 subd. 8).
A licensee SHALL NOT DISCOURAGE prospective parties from SEEKING THE SERVICES OF AN ATTORNEY (82.81 subd. 11).

EXCLUSIVE AGREEMENTS: a licensee may not negotiate the sale, exchange, lease or listing DIRECTLY WITH AN OWNER KNOWING the owner has an EXCLUSIVE written contract with another broker for the same service, nor negotiate with a buyer knowing the buyer has such a contract. A licensee may not INDUCE ANY PARTY to BREACH a contract, option, listing, buyer's agreement or facilitator services agreement (82.81 subd. 9(a), (b)).

THE EXCEPTION: a licensee MAY discuss terms for a future contract to begin AFTER the existing exclusive contract EXPIRES, WHEN THE INQUIRY OR DISCUSSION IS INITIATED BY the owner, lessor, buyer or lessee - AND THE LICENSEE MUST ASK whether such an exclusive contract exists (82.81 subd. 9(c)).

When the OWNER fails or is unable to consummate, THROUGH NO FAULT OF THE PURCHASER, the listing broker MAY NOT CLAIM ANY PORTION of the purchaser's trust funds absent a SEPARATE AGREEMENT WITH THE PURCHASER (82.81 subd. 3).
No licensee may ENGAGE OR AUTHORISE AN UNLICENSED PERSON to act as a broker, salesperson or closing agent on the licensee's behalf (82.81 subd. 4).

A chapter 82 licence does NOT authorise dealing in VENDOR'S INTERESTS IN CONTRACTS FOR DEED, MORTGAGEE'S INTERESTS IN MORTGAGES or other evidence of real-estate indebtedness - except that a licensee representing a party in the sale, lease or exchange MAY arrange the sale of such an instrument for the subject property IF THERE IS NO COMPENSATION BEYOND THE BROKERAGE COMMISSION (82.81 subd. 7).

FRAUDULENT, DECEPTIVE OR DISHONEST PRACTICES (82.81 subd. 12) also include: violating ANY STATE OR FEDERAL DISCRIMINATION LAW protecting purchasers or renters; MAKING A MATERIAL MISSTATEMENT in a licence application or in information furnished to the Commissioner; PROCURING A LICENCE by fraud; MAKING ANY MATERIAL MISREPRESENTATION or PERMITTING ANOTHER TO; making FALSE OR MISLEADING STATEMENTS likely to influence or induce a transaction; FAILING WITHIN A REASONABLE TIME to account for or remit money belonging to another; COMMINGLING; DEMANDING A COMMISSION FROM A SELLER KNOWING the licensee is NOT ENTITLED to it; FAILING TO MAINTAIN A TRUST ACCOUNT at all times; and engaging in ANTICOMPETITIVE ACTIVITY with respect to the offer, sale or rental of real estate.

A licensee is DEEMED to have violated the section if FOUND BY A FINAL COURT DECISION to have violated Minnesota's ANTITRUST sections 325D.49 to 325D.66 (82.81 subd. 12(b)). The Commissioner's authority is NOT LIMITED to the practices the section lists (82.81 subd. 12(c)).

FINANCIAL PLANNING: a licensee may not represent that they are engaged in the business of FINANCIAL PLANNING unless they give the client a SIGNED DISCLOSURE DOCUMENT, leaving a copy with the client, in the statutory wording covering the basis of compensation, the firms whose products are offered, the licences held, and the specific products the licensee may sell (82.81 subd. 12(a)(17)).

l: The Commissioner may by ORDER DENY, SUSPEND OR REVOKE a licence, or CENSURE a licensee, on finding that the order is IN THE PUBLIC INTEREST and that the applicant or licensee - or, for a broker, any officer, director, partner, employee, agent or controlling person - has done one of the listed things (82.82 subd. 1).

THE GROUNDS: filing an application INCOMPLETE IN ANY MATERIAL RESPECT or containing a FALSE OR MISLEADING statement of material fact; engaging in a FRAUDULENT, DECEPTIVE OR DISHONEST PRACTICE; being ENJOINED by a court from conduct involving any aspect of the real estate business; FAILING TO REASONABLY SUPERVISE brokers, salespersons or closing agents SO AS TO CAUSE INJURY OR HARM TO THE PUBLIC; violating any provision of chapter 82 or any rule or order; being shown to be INCOMPETENT, UNTRUSTWORTHY OR FINANCIALLY IRRESPONSIBLE in conducting the licensed business; ACTING FOR A PARTY WHERE THE LICENSEE HAS A CONFLICT OF INTEREST that may affect the ability to represent that party, WITHOUT THE PARTY'S KNOWLEDGE AND CONSENT; and violating chapter 58 while performing residential mortgage activities.

PROCEDURE: the Commissioner ISSUES AN ORDER TO SHOW CAUSE stating the SPECIFIC STATUTE OR RULE violated and giving reasonable notice of the hearing. The Commissioner MAY SUMMARILY SUSPEND a licence PENDING FINAL DETERMINATION - and then a HEARING ON THE MERITS MUST BE HELD WITHIN 30 DAYS of the suspension order. Hearings follow CHAPTER 14, and FAILURE TO APPEAR after due notice is a DEFAULT in which the allegations MAY BE DEEMED TRUE (82.82 subd. 5).

The Commissioner MAY DELEGATE the hearing to an ADMINISTRATIVE LAW JUDGE, who makes PROPOSED FINDINGS OF FACT and has the same power as the Commissioner to compel witnesses, examine them under oath, require production and issue subpoenas (82.82 subd. 6). Orders are subject to JUDICIAL REVIEW under chapter 14 (82.82 subd. 7).

THE COMMISSIONER SHALL NOT COERCE OR ATTEMPT TO COERCE a licensee into a MONETARY SETTLEMENT with a consumer during a complaint investigation - though the Commissioner may weigh the licensee's efforts to MITIGATE the consumer's losses in setting the sanction (82.82 subd. 4).

The Commissioner may REVOKE a licence or DENY an application on finding the licensee IS NO LONGER IN EXISTENCE, HAS CEASED TO DO BUSINESS, is subject to an ADJUDICATION OF MENTAL INCOMPETENCE or to a committee, conservator or guardian, or CANNOT BE LOCATED AFTER REASONABLE SEARCH (82.82 subd. 10).

WITHDRAWAL: a licensee may ask to withdraw from licensee status; it takes effect 30 DAYS after receipt unless a proceeding is pending or begun within those 30 days, and after an automatic withdrawal the Commissioner may still begin a revocation or suspension proceeding WITHIN ONE YEAR (82.63 subd. 15).
CRIMINAL PENALTY: any person who violates any provision of chapter 82 or any rule or order of the Commissioner is GUILTY OF A GROSS MISDEMEANOR (82.83).

CIVIL ACTIONS FOR COMPENSATION: no one may sue for compensation for acts requiring a licence WITHOUT ALLEGING AND PROVING they were DULY LICENSED WHEN THE CAUSE OF ACTION AROSE (82.85 subd. 1); no one may sue for a commission on real property WITHOUT A WRITTEN AGREEMENT (82.85 subd. 2); and no one may sue for a commission on RESIDENTIAL property unless their AGENCY RELATIONSHIPS WERE DISCLOSED as the chapter requires (82.85 subd. 3).
The Commissioner may PUBLISH information to assist in administering the chapter or to EDUCATE AND PROTECT THE PUBLIC about fraudulent, deceptive or dishonest practices (82.84).

vocab: Override clause
The provision letting a broker claim a commission after expiration on a sale to someone on the protective list; capped at six months, or two years on a business sale (82.66).
Protective list
The list of prospects or properties the licensee must furnish within 72 hours of expiration to enforce an override clause, with the burden of proof on the licensee (82.66).
Broker price opinion

A licensee's written opinion of price, which may never be the primary basis of value for originating a residential mortgage on a principal dwelling, and which must carry the statutory not-an-appraisal disclaimer (82.735).
Guaranteed sale program
A programme under which the broker buys the property if it does not sell, requiring written disclosure of terms and of profit disposition before the listing is signed (82.74).
Order to show cause
The Commissioner's charging document, which must state the specific statute or rule violated; a summary suspension may accompany it (82.82 subd. 5).
Censure
A sanction short of suspension or revocation that the Commissioner may impose (82.82 subd. 1).

sections.h: Recording, Torrens and the transfer taxes (chapters 508, 287)
l: Minnesota has TWO TITLE SYSTEMS. ABSTRACT property is recorded with the COUNTY RECORDER. TORRENS property - registered land under CHAPTER 508 - is handled by the REGISTRAR OF TITLES, which issues a CERTIFICATE OF TITLE that is conclusive as to the interests noted on it.

The DEED TAX (287.21) is imposed on each deed or instrument conveying real property in this state, AGAINST THE NET CONSIDERATION. The rate is .0033 OF THE NET CONSIDERATION when the consideration, excluding the value of any lien or encumbrance remaining at the time of sale, EXCEEDS $3,000. When there is NO CONSIDERATION, or consideration of $3,000 OR LESS, or for consolidations, mergers or designated transfers, THE TAX IS $1.65.
The deed tax is DUE WHEN THE TAXABLE DEED IS PRESENTED FOR RECORDING (287.21 subd. 1(d)).

The MORTGAGE REGISTRY TAX (287.035) is imposed ON THE PRIVILEGE OF RECORDING A MORTGAGE, at .0023 OF THE DEBT or portion of the debt secured by a recorded mortgage of Minnesota real property. THE PERSON LIABLE IS THE MORTGAGOR. The tax is NOT imposed on lawful INTEREST that may accrue on the debt.
A CERTIFICATE OF VALUE under 272.115 accompanies the recording of a taxable conveyance, and the WELL DISCLOSURE CERTIFICATE rules hang off that same requirement (103I.235 subd. 1(h)).

An agreement for the sale of land, or a listing or buyer's agreement, must be in writing to be enforceable - and 82.85 subd. 2 independently bars a commission suit without a WRITTEN AGREEMENT.

l: It is an UNFAIR DISCRIMINATORY PRACTICE for an owner, lessee, sublessee, assignee or MANAGING AGENT, or ANY AGENT OF THESE, to REFUSE TO SELL, RENT OR LEASE, or otherwise deny or withhold any real property, because of a protected class.

MINNESOTA'S PROTECTED CLASSES FOR REAL PROPERTY: RACE, COLOR, CREED, RELIGION, NATIONAL ORIGIN, SEX, GENDER IDENTITY, MARITAL STATUS, STATUS WITH REGARD TO PUBLIC ASSISTANCE, DISABILITY, SEXUAL ORIENTATION and FAMILIAL STATUS.

Minnesota therefore goes BEYOND the federal Fair Housing Act, which covers race, color, religion, national origin, sex, disability and familial status. The MINNESOTA ADDITIONS are CREED, GENDER IDENTITY, MARITAL STATUS, STATUS WITH REGARD TO PUBLIC ASSISTANCE and SEXUAL ORIENTATION. "Status with regard to public assistance" is what makes refusing a Section 8 voucher a problem in Minnesota.

It is equally an unfair discriminatory practice to DISCRIMINATE IN THE TERMS, CONDITIONS OR PRIVILEGES of a sale, rental or lease, or in the FURNISHING OF FACILITIES OR SERVICES - although REASONABLE RULES INTENDED TO PROTECT THE SAFETY OF MINORS in their use of the property or its facilities are not prohibited.

ADVERTISING: it is an unfair discriminatory practice to PRINT, CIRCULATE OR POST any advertisement or sign, to USE ANY FORM OF APPLICATION, or to MAKE ANY RECORD OR INQUIRY in connection with a prospective purchase, rental or lease, that EXPRESSES DIRECTLY OR INDIRECTLY any limitation, specification or discrimination as to a protected class, or any intent to make one.
The administering agency is the MINNESOTA DEPARTMENT OF HUMAN RIGHTS (chapter 363A).

VIOLATING ANY STATE OR FEDERAL DISCRIMINATION LAW intended to protect the rights of purchasers or renters of real estate is itself a FRAUDULENT, DECEPTIVE OR DISHONEST PRACTICE under the licence law (82.81 subd. 12(a)(4)), and COMPLIANCE with fair housing is a continuing education requirement every licence period (82.61(c)(2)).

A licensee may not knowingly induce or attempt to induce discriminatory conduct through these channels, and the licence law's own remedies - denial, suspension, revocation or censure - run alongside the Human Rights Act's.

l: BEFORE SIGNING AN AGREEMENT TO SELL OR TRANSFER residential real property, THE SELLER must make a WRITTEN DISCLOSURE to the prospective buyer of ALL MATERIAL FACTS OF WHICH THE SELLER IS AWARE that could ADVERSELY AND SIGNIFICANTLY AFFECT an ordinary buyer's use and enjoyment of the property, or any INTENDED USE of which the seller is aware (513.55 subd. 1(a)).

The disclosure must be made IN GOOD FAITH AND BASED UPON THE BEST OF THE SELLER'S KNOWLEDGE at the time (513.55 subd. 1(b)). Minnesota's duty is a GENERAL MATERIAL-FACTS DISCLOSURE, not a mandated checklist form.

The seller MAY deliver the written disclosure to the REAL ESTATE LICENSEE REPRESENTING OR ASSISTING THE PROSPECTIVE BUYER, and that IS CONSIDERED TO HAVE BEEN PROVIDED TO THE BUYER - but THE LICENSEE MUST THEN GIVE A COPY TO THE BUYER (513.55 subd. 2).

THE INSPECTION ALTERNATIVE: a seller need NOT disclose information if a WRITTEN REPORT disclosing it was PREPARED BY A QUALIFIED THIRD PARTY and provided to the prospective buyer - BUT the seller MUST disclose MATERIAL FACTS KNOWN TO THE SELLER THAT CONTRADICT the report if given a copy of it (513.56 subd. 3).

NOT REQUIRED TO BE DISCLOSED, by statute: occupancy by someone suspected to be HIV-infected or diagnosed with AIDS; that the property was the SITE OF A SUICIDE, ACCIDENTAL DEATH, NATURAL DEATH OR PERCEIVED PARANORMAL ACTIVITY; and that it is in a NEIGHBOURHOOD CONTAINING AN ADULT FAMILY HOME, COMMUNITY-BASED RESIDENTIAL FACILITY OR NURSING HOME (513.56 subd. 1).

PREDATORY OFFENDERS and AIRPORT ZONING: no duty to disclose, provided the seller timely gives the corresponding WRITTEN NOTICE pointing to local law enforcement or the Department of Corrections, or to the county recorder's office (513.56 subd. 2, subd. 3(c)).

FOURTEEN EXCEPTIONS to the whole disclosure requirement (513.54), including: property that is NOT RESIDENTIAL; a GRATUITOUS TRANSFER; a transfer by COURT ORDER; a transfer to a GOVERNMENT or governmental agency; a transfer by FORECLOSURE OR DEED IN LIEU; a transfer to HEIRS OR DEVISEES of a decedent; a transfer FROM A COTENANT TO OTHER COTENANTS; a transfer to a SPOUSE, PARENT, GRANDPARENT, CHILD OR GRANDCHILD; a transfer between spouses from a DIVORCE DECREE or incidental property settlement; NEWLY CONSTRUCTED RESIDENTIAL PROPERTY THAT HAS NOT BEEN INHABITED; an UNEXERCISED OPTION on a common interest community unit; and a TRANSFER TO A TENANT IN POSSESSION.

LIABILITY: a seller is NOT LIABLE for an error, inaccuracy or omission that was NOT WITHIN THE SELLER'S PERSONAL KNOWLEDGE, or was based entirely on information from a qualified third party where ORDINARY CARE WAS EXERCISED in transmitting it. It is NOT a violation to fail to disclose what could be found ONLY by INSPECTING INACCESSIBLE PORTIONS of the property, or ONLY BY SOMEONE WITH EXPERTISE beyond the seller's knowledge (513.57 subd. 1).

A seller WHO WAS AWARE of material facts and failed to disclose IS LIABLE to the buyer, who may recover DAMAGES and equitable relief. THE ACTION MUST BE COMMENCED WITHIN TWO YEARS AFTER THE DATE THE BUYER CLOSED the purchase or transfer (513.57 subd. 2). Nothing precludes an action for FRAUD OR NEGLIGENT MISREPRESENTATION (513.57 subd. 3).

WAIVER: the written disclosure MAY BE WAIVED IF THE SELLER AND THE PROSPECTIVE BUYER AGREE IN WRITING - but waiving it does NOT waive, limit or abridge any disclosure obligation created by ANY OTHER LAW, such as the well and septic disclosures (513.60).
The licensee's own 82.68 subd. 3 duty is SEPARATE and is NOT waived by the seller's waiver.

sections.h: Wells, septic systems and underground tanks
l: WELL DISCLOSURE (103I.235): BEFORE SIGNING AN AGREEMENT TO SELL OR TRANSFER real property, the SELLER MUST DISCLOSE IN WRITING information about the STATUS AND LOCATION OF ALL KNOWN WELLS - either a statement that the seller KNOWS OF NO WELLS, or a disclosure statement giving the LEGAL DESCRIPTION AND COUNTY and A MAP drawn from available information showing each well's location so far as practicable. For each well the seller must state whether it is IN USE, NOT IN USE, OR SEALED.

AT CLOSING, that information plus the BUYER'S NAME AND MAILING ADDRESS and the QUARTILE, SECTION, TOWNSHIP AND RANGE of each well must appear on a WELL DISCLOSURE CERTIFICATE SIGNED BY THE SELLER or an authorised person.
NO CERTIFICATE IS NEEDED if the seller knows of no wells AND the deed contains the statement: "The Seller certifies that the Seller does not know of any wells on the described real property."
ON A CONTRACT FOR DEED, the certificate at the time the deed is given is signed BY THE BUYER (the grantee), with the equivalent no-wells certification available on the deed.

RECORDING CONSEQUENCE: a county recorder or registrar of titles MAY NOT RECORD a deed requiring a certificate of value unless the deed carries the no-wells statement or is accompanied by a completed well disclosure certificate. The recorder COLLECTS A $54 FEE for a completed certificate and TRANSMITS $46.50 of it to the COMMISSIONER OF HEALTH, who keeps the certificate AT LEAST SIX YEARS. The certificate ITSELF IS NOT FILED OR RECORDED in the county's records.

If the seller FAILS to provide a required certificate, THE BUYER may sign one based on the disclosure statement or other available information. NO NEW CERTIFICATE is needed if the deed carries a certification that the STATUS AND NUMBER OF WELLS HAVE NOT CHANGED since the last filed certificate.
FAILURE TO COMPLY DOES NOT IMPAIR the validity of the deed between the parties, nor the record as notice (103I.235 subd. 1(k)) - the sanction is elsewhere, including subd. 2 liability.

SUBSURFACE SEWAGE TREATMENT SYSTEMS (115.55 subd. 6): BEFORE SIGNING AN AGREEMENT TO SELL OR TRANSFER real property, the seller must DISCLOSE IN WRITING HOW SEWAGE GENERATED AT THE PROPERTY IS MANAGED - by delivering a statement that either the sewage GOES TO A FACILITY PERMITTED BY THE AGENCY, or that it DOES NOT and is therefore SUBJECT TO APPLICABLE REQUIREMENTS.

LEAKING UNDERGROUND STORAGE TANKS: the outline cites the POLLUTION CONTROL AGENCY provisions at 116.46 to 116.48 and the PETROLEUM TANK RELEASE CLEANUP provisions at 115C.01 to 115C.09. Tanks must be registered and releases reported, and the Petrofund reimburses eligible cleanup costs. For a licensee, a known or suspected tank or release is the kind of fact that must be disclosed under 82.68 subd. 3(a) if the licensee is aware it could adversely and significantly affect use or enjoyment.
Note the pattern: WELL, SEPTIC AND TANK disclosures are their OWN statutory duties. A written waiver of the 513.55 general disclosure does NOT touch them (513.60).

Statutory warranties: ONE year workmanship and materials, TWO years systems installation, TEN years major construction defects.
Minnesota's fair housing classes add CREED, GENDER IDENTITY, MARITAL STATUS, PUBLIC ASSISTANCE STATUS and SEXUAL ORIENTATION to the federal list.
The seller's 513.55 disclosure CAN be waived in writing - unusual among the states - but the well and septic disclosures cannot ride along.
Suicide, natural death and perceived paranormal activity need not be disclosed by the seller either.
The 513.57 limitation period is TWO YEARS FROM CLOSING.
Newly constructed, never-inhabited property is EXEMPT from the seller disclosure.

The .0023 tax on the debt secured by a recorded mortgage, payable by the mortgagor (287.035).

The date from which the one-, two- and ten-year statutory home warranties run (327A.02).

A Minnesota protected class with no federal counterpart, which is why refusing a housing voucher is a Human Rights Act problem (363A.09).

Qualified third party

A contract for deed buyer from 2021 misses three payments. The seller is an individual, not an investor seller.

l: Minnesota has TWO foreclosure routes: FORECLOSURE BY ADVERTISEMENT under CHAPTER 580, which is the common non-judicial route used where the mortgage contains a power of sale, and FORECLOSURE BY ACTION under CHAPTER 581, the judicial route. CHAPTER 582 holds general provisions applying to both.

REDEMPTION BY THE MORTGAGOR (580.23 subd. 1): after a sale in conformity with chapter 580, the mortgagor, the mortgagor's personal representatives or assigns may redeem WITHIN SIX MONTHS AFTER THE SALE by paying the SUM FOR WHICH THE PROPERTY WAS SOLD, WITH INTEREST from the time of sale at the rate stated in the certificate of sale - or at SIX PERCENT PER ANNUM if the certificate states no rate - together with any further sums payable under 582.03 and 582.031.

Delivery of redemption funds and documents must be made at the recipient's NORMAL PLACE OF BUSINESS, on days OTHER THAN SUNDAY, SATURDAY AND LEGAL HOLIDAYS, BETWEEN 9:00 A.M. AND 4:00 P.M. (580.23 subd. 1(b)).

Regardless of the redemption period's length, THE SHERIFF MAY ACCEPT A SPECIFIC SUM LESS THAN THE FULL AMOUNT DUE if, before the period expires, the sheriff receives WRITTEN CONFIRMATION from the holder of the sheriff's certificate, or that holder's attorney, that the holder has agreed to accept it (580.23 subd. 1(c)).

A TWELVE-MONTH REDEMPTION PERIOD applies instead in listed cases (580.23 subd. 2), including where the MORTGAGE WAS EXECUTED BEFORE JULY 1, 1967, and where the AMOUNT CLAIMED DUE as of the date of the notice of foreclosure sale is LESS THAN 66-2/3 PERCENT OF THE ORIGINAL PRINCIPAL AMOUNT secured by the mortgage.
So the default answer is SIX MONTHS, with twelve months as the exception - the reverse of what a candidate who learned another state's law may expect.

l: A CONTRACT FOR DEED is the vendor-financed instrument in which the seller retains legal title until the purchase price is paid. On DEFAULT giving the seller a right to terminate, the seller terminates by SERVING A NOTICE on the purchaser specifying the conditions in default.

FOR CONTRACTS EXECUTED ON OR AFTER AUGUST 1, 1985, the notice must state that THE CONTRACT WILL TERMINATE 60 DAYS AFTER SERVICE OF THE NOTICE - or a shorter period allowed, or a longer period required, by subdivision 4 - unless the purchase cures before the termination date (559.21 subd. 2a).

A CONTRACT FOR DEED EXECUTED BY AN INVESTOR SELLER IS TERMINATED ON 90 DAYS' NOTICE, and NO NOTICE MAY BE GIVEN for such a contract unless, AT LEAST 30 DAYS BEFORE SERVICE, some part of the conditions of default has existed AND the investor seller has notified the purchaser of those conditions BY CERTIFIED MAIL to the purchaser's last known address (559.21 subd. 4(a), (f)).

EARNEST MONEY CONTRACTS, PURCHASE AGREEMENTS AND EXERCISED OPTIONS subject to the section may, unless their terms provide a longer period, be TERMINATED ON 30 DAYS' NOTICE, or may be CANCELLED UNDER SECTION 559.217 (559.21 subd. 4(a)(1)).

OLDER CONTRACTS use graduated periods based on how much of the price has been paid - for example a contract executed on or after May 1, 1980 and before August 1, 1985 terminates 30 days after service if less than TEN PERCENT has been paid, 60 days if ten percent or more but less than TWENTY-FIVE PERCENT, and 90 days if twenty-five percent or more.

TO CURE, the purchaser must comply with the conditions in default, pay the costs of service, and PAY AN AMOUNT TOWARD ATTORNEY'S FEES actually expended or incurred - $1,000 for contracts executed on or after AUGUST 1, 2024 (earlier contracts use the older $250/$500 and $125/$250 tiers) - except that NO ATTORNEY'S FEE AMOUNT IS REQUIRED unless some part of the default HAS EXISTED FOR AT LEAST 30 DAYS BEFORE SERVICE of the notice.

The statutory notice is REQUIRED NOTWITHSTANDING ANY CONTRARY PROVISION IN THE CONTRACT (559.21 subd. 4(a)). Service is made IN THE SAME MANNER AS A SUMMONS in district court; outside the state in the same manner without a sheriff's return of not found.

SERVICE BY PUBLICATION is available against a resident who has left the state or cannot be found, or a nonresident or foreign entity: THREE WEEKS' PUBLISHED NOTICE has the same effect as personal service, and the published notice must state that the person has 90 DAYS AFTER THE FIRST DATE OF PUBLICATION to comply and that the contract terminates 90 days after that date. If the real estate is ACTUALLY OCCUPIED, a person in possession must ALSO be personally served within 30 DAYS after first publication, and if an address is known a copy must be MAILED within 30 days by first class mail (559.21 subd. 4(b)).

l: THE HOMESTEAD EXEMPTION (chapter 510) protects the debtor's homestead from seizure or sale on most judgments and creditors' claims, up to statutory value and area limits. It is a CREDITOR-PROTECTION rule, distinct from the HOMESTEAD CLASSIFICATION that reduces property tax and from the 507.02 SPOUSAL SIGNATURE rule - the exam likes to blur the three.
The homestead exemption does NOT defeat a mortgage the owner granted, nor taxes and assessments, nor a mechanic's lien for work on the homestead itself.
MECHANIC'S LIENS (chapter 514) secure payment to those who CONTRIBUTE LABOR, SKILL, MATERIAL OR MACHINERY to the improvement of real estate. The lien attaches to the improvement and to the land.

Minnesota mechanic's liens take PRIORITY FROM THE FIRST VISIBLE BEGINNING of the improvement on the ground, which is why all of a project's lien claimants share the same priority date regardless of when each one started - and why a lender's mortgage recorded after work has visibly begun can be subordinate.

A lien claimant must serve the required PRELIEN NOTICE where applicable, record a LIEN STATEMENT within the statutory period after the claimant's last contribution, and bring suit within the statutory period thereafter or the lien expires.

For a licensee the practical point is disclosure and title: unrecorded lien rights arising from recent visible improvements are an encumbrance risk a buyer's title work must address, and known facts about them fall within the licensee's 82.68 subd. 3(a) material-facts duty.

LIENS GENERALLY: the outline's financial-instruments block also expects familiarity with how liens are satisfied at closing out of the seller's proceeds, and with the closing statement the listing broker must deliver if acting as the transaction closing agent (82.71 subd. 5).

mn/finance.summary: Five items. Minnesota's foreclosure runs by ADVERTISEMENT with a SIX-MONTH redemption period, contracts for deed are cancelled on a 60-DAY notice, and the homestead exemption and mechanic's liens round it out.
traps: Redemption is SIX MONTHS as the default. Twelve months is the exception, not the rule.
Contract for deed cancellation is 60 DAYS for ordinary contracts, 90 DAYS for an INVESTOR SELLER, 30 DAYS for a purchase agreement.
An investor seller must have sent a certified-mail default notice 30 days BEFORE serving the cancellation notice.
Mechanic's lien priority dates from the FIRST VISIBLE BEGINNING of the improvement - not from each claimant's own start.
Three different homestead ideas: the SPOUSAL SIGNATURE rule (507.02), the CREDITOR EXEMPTION (ch. 510) and the TAX CLASSIFICATION. Keep them apart.
vocab: Foreclosure by advertisement

Sheriff's certificate

Contract for deed
A vendor-financed sale in which the seller keeps legal title until paid, cancellable on 60 days' statutory notice for contracts executed after 1 August 1985 (559.21).
Investor seller
A contract for deed seller whose contracts terminate only on 90 days' notice, preceded by a certified-mail default notice 30 days earlier (559.21 subd. 4).
First visible beginning
The moment that fixes mechanic's lien priority for an entire improvement in Minnesota (chapter 514).

mn/interests.blurb: Spousal conveyance, subdivided land, condominiums and common interest communities, property taxes, landlord and tenant.
examples: A husband holds title to the family home in his name alone and signs a purchase agreement without his wife.
The conveyance of the HOMESTEAD is not valid without both spouses' signatures. The wife must sign the deed, or sign a separate conveyance relinquishing her rights (507.02).
A condominium owner lists their unit. When do the association documents have to reach the buyer?

Before execution of any purchase agreement, or otherwise before conveyance - the declaration, articles, bylaws, rules, fines list and collection policy, a resale disclosure certificate no more than 90 days old, and any reserve study from the past three years (515B.4-107).

l: If the owner is MARRIED, NO CONVEYANCE OF THE HOMESTEAD IS VALID WITHOUT THE SIGNATURES OF BOTH SPOUSES. This is the single most tested Minnesota ownership rule.
THREE EXCEPTIONS: a MORTGAGE FOR PURCHASE MONEY under 507.03; a CONVEYANCE BETWEEN SPOUSES under 500.19 subd. 4; and a SEVERANCE OF A JOINT TENANCY under 500.19 subd. 5.
A spouse's signature MAY BE MADE BY THE SPOUSE'S DULY APPOINTED ATTORNEY-IN-FACT.

Spouses may convey the real estate of either BY THEIR JOINT DEED. A spouse may, BY SEPARATE DEED, convey ANY REAL ESTATE OWNED BY THAT SPOUSE EXCEPT THE HOMESTEAD, subject to the other spouse's rights - and either spouse may by separate conveyance RELINQUISH ALL RIGHTS in real estate conveyed by the other.

Either spouse may separately appoint an ATTORNEY-IN-FACT to sell or convey real estate owned by that spouse or to join a conveyance made by or for the other spouse. Use of a power of attorney is subject to 518.58 subd. 1a.
A MINOR SPOUSE HAS LEGAL CAPACITY to join in a conveyance of real estate owned by the other spouse, so long as the minor spouse is not incapacitated for some reason other than minority.

l: Minnesota has THREE condominium-era statutes: chapter 515 (the older Minnesota Condominium Act), chapter 515A (the Uniform Condominium Act), and chapter 515B, the MINNESOTA COMMON INTEREST OWNERSHIP ACT (MCIOA), which governs CONDOMINIUMS, COOPERATIVES AND PLANNED COMMUNITIES.

RESALE OF A UNIT (515B.4-107): on a resale by a unit owner OTHER THAN A DECLARANT, unless exempt under 515B.4-101(c), the owner must FURNISH THE PURCHASER, BEFORE EXECUTION OF ANY PURCHASE AGREEMENT or otherwise before conveyance: copies of the DECLARATION (other than the CIC plat), the ARTICLES OF INCORPORATION and BYLAWS, any RULES AND REGULATIONS, and any amendments or supplemental declarations, including the list of COMMON FINES AND ALLOWABLE REMEDIES and the association's COLLECTION POLICY.

Also required: the MASTER DECLARATION and its documents if the community is subject to one; a RESALE DISCLOSURE CERTIFICATE from the association DATED NOT MORE THAN 90 DAYS before the purchase agreement or the conveyance, WHICHEVER IS EARLIER; and A COPY OF ANY RESERVE STUDY the association obtained WITHIN THE PAST THREE YEARS for evaluating the adequacy of replacement reserve contributions.
The ASSOCIATION MUST FURNISH THE CERTIFICATE WITHIN TEN DAYS after a unit owner's (or their representative's) request, and MAY CHARGE A REASONABLE FEE for it and the related documents.
A unit owner who provides a certificate IS NOT LIABLE TO THE PURCHASER FOR ERRONEOUS INFORMATION THE ASSOCIATION SUPPLIED and included in it.

A unit owner who took title through FORECLOSURE OR A DEED IN LIEU must tell the association, when requesting the certificate, WHETHER THEY ARE A DECLARANT - and THE UNIT OWNER, NOT THE ASSOCIATION, is liable for any loss from an incorrect representation of declarant status.

The WELL DISCLOSURE requirement does NOT apply to the sale of an INDIVIDUAL CONDOMINIUM UNIT under chapters 515 and 515B; for COMMON AREAS the association or other responsible person reports well locations and status to the commissioner and must notify them WITHIN 30 DAYS of any change in reported status (103I.235 subd. 1(e), (f)).

l: Chapter 83, the MINNESOTA SUBDIVIDED LAND SALES PRACTICES ACT (83.20 to 83.45), governs the offer and sale of SUBDIVIDED LAND - generally land divided or proposed to be divided into lots or parcels for sale as part of a common promotional plan.

Subdivided land must generally be REGISTERED with the Commissioner before it is offered or sold, with a PUBLIC OFFERING STATEMENT given to purchasers, unless an EXEMPTION applies. The Commissioner may issue stop orders, deny or revoke registrations and seek injunctions.

Every real estate OFFICE AND BRANCH OFFICE must keep a current copy of CHAPTER 83 as well as chapter 82 and the rules available for licensees' use (82.73 subd. 1) - the exam expects you to know chapter 83 exists and is part of the licensee's reference shelf.

PROPERTY TAXES: Minnesota real property taxes are PAYABLE IN THE YEAR AFTER THE ASSESSMENT YEAR, and delinquency and enforcement run under CHAPTER 279. Unpaid taxes become a lien and proceed through judgment and forfeiture.

SPECIAL ASSESSMENTS for local improvements are levied by the municipality against benefited property and, like taxes, run with the land until paid. A prospective buyer's exposure to a PENDING OR LEVIED special assessment is the kind of fact a licensee must disclose if the licensee is aware it could adversely and significantly affect use or enjoyment (82.68 subd. 3(a)).
The DEED TAX and the MORTGAGE REGISTRY TAX (chapter 287) are the transfer-side taxes, covered under conveyance procedures.

l: Chapter 504B governs RESIDENTIAL LANDLORD AND TENANT law in Minnesota, including security deposits, the covenants of habitability, and eviction actions.

SECURITY DEPOSITS (504B.178): any money whose function is to SECURE PERFORMANCE of a residential rental agreement - other than money that is EXCLUSIVELY AN ADVANCE PAYMENT OF RENT - is governed by the section.

Such a deposit is NOT considered received IN A FIDUCIARY CAPACITY within the meaning of 82.55 subd. 26, but is HELD BY THE LANDLORD FOR THE TENANT and bears SIMPLE NONCOMPOUNDED INTEREST AT ONE PERCENT PER ANNUM.

Interest is computed from the FIRST DAY OF THE NEXT MONTH FOLLOWING FULL PAYMENT of the deposit to the LAST DAY OF THE MONTH in which the landlord in good faith complies with the return requirements, or to the DATE JUDGMENT IS ENTERED in a civil action over the deposit - WHICHEVER IS EARLIER. ANY INTEREST AMOUNT LESS THAN $1 IS EXCLUDED.
A broker MAY establish and maintain INTEREST-BEARING ACCOUNTS for receiving such deposits in accordance with 504B.178 (82.75 subd. 7).

PROPERTY MANAGEMENT AND THE BROKER'S SUPERVISION: a broker is NOT responsible for supervising, and a licensee is not responsible for operating within the brokerage, activities that would be PROPERTY MANAGEMENT - leasing, maintenance and repair - so long as the real estate is INDIVIDUALLY OWNED (the licensee holds an ownership interest) or ENTITY-OWNED (owned by a corporation, LLC, partnership or trust in which the licensee holds an ownership interest as owner, trustee, partner, officer or other beneficiary) (82.73 subd. 3(e)).

A RENTAL SERVICE must obtain a REAL ESTATE BROKER'S LICENCE before engaging in business, and no one may act as a salesperson for a rental service without a salesperson's licence. A rental service may NOT provide information about a rental unit WITHOUT THE EXPRESS AUTHORITY OF THE OWNER, and may not advertise MISLEADINGLY about fees, services, availability or rental terms (82.78).

A buyer wins a $200,000 judgment against a salesperson for converting their earnest money, and cannot collect.

The fund pays actual and direct out-of-pocket loss, excluding attorney's fees and interest, capped at $150,000 for that claimant on that transaction - and no more than $250,000 in total against that licensee. A salesperson quits on 1 March with four months left in the licence period.

Their licence is ineffective at once, the broker must notify the Commissioner within ten days, and the salesperson may apply to transfer to another broker any time in the rest of the period. After that, a new licence application is required (82.63 subd. 6).

l: A salesperson applicant must complete a Commissioner-approved COURSE OF 30 HOURS OF INSTRUCTION - COURSE I - BEFORE TAKING THE EXAMINATION.

The applicant must then complete AN ADDITIONAL 60 HOURS - COURSE II AND COURSE III - BEFORE FILING THE APPLICATION for the licence. Of those 60 hours, THREE HOURS must be STATE AND FEDERAL FAIR HOUSING law and TWO HOURS must be LAWS AND REGULATIONS ON AGENCY REPRESENTATION AND DISCLOSURE (82.59 subd. 8(a)).
A PASSING GRADE is 75 PERCENT OR HIGHER ON THE UNIFORM PORTION AND 75 PERCENT OR HIGHER ON THE STATE PORTION - the portions are scored separately (82.59 subd. 6).
The Commissioner WILL NOT ACCEPT the score of a person who CHEATED, and cheating is a ground for DENYING the application (82.59 subd. 6).
NO APPLICANT IS ELIGIBLE TO TAKE ANY EXAMINATION if a broker's or salesperson's licence HAS BEEN REVOKED IN THIS OR ANY OTHER STATE WITHIN TWO YEARS of the date of application (82.59 subd. 2).
Examinations are held AT LEAST EVERY 45 DAYS (82.59 subd. 3).

A BROKER applicant must have A MINIMUM OF THREE YEARS of actual experience WITHIN THE PREVIOUS FIVE-YEAR PERIOD as a licensed salesperson in this or a comparable state, or be otherwise similarly qualified in the Commissioner's opinion, and must complete a 30-HOUR BROKER COURSE - 3 hours of it fair housing - WITHIN 12 MONTHS BEFORE the date of application (82.59 subd. 4, subd. 8(b)).
The broker's examination must be MORE EXACTING than the salesperson's (82.59 subd. 4(a)).

The Commissioner MAY WAIVE the broker experience requirement for someone with a REAL ESTATE DEGREE from an accredited college or university, a PRACTISING ATTORNEY whose practice involves real estate law, or a PUBLIC OFFICER whose duties involve real estate law or transactions. A waiver LAPSES if the applicant does not pass the broker's examination WITHIN ONE YEAR of the grant (82.59 subd. 5).
The Department of Commerce's own licence guide adds that the application must be filed WITHIN ONE YEAR OF PASSING the examination, or the examination must be retaken.

l: Every salesperson and broker must complete 30 HOURS of approved real estate continuing education, AS A STUDENT OR LECTURER, DURING THE INITIAL LICENCE PERIOD AND DURING EACH SUCCEEDING 24-MONTH LICENCE PERIOD.
AT LEAST 15 OF THE 30 HOURS MUST BE COMPLETED DURING THE FIRST 12 MONTHS of the 24-month period. This front-loading is the rule candidates most often get wrong.

Each licence period must include AT LEAST ONE HOUR on LAWS OR REGULATIONS ON AGENCY REPRESENTATION AND DISCLOSURE, and AT LEAST ONE HOUR on STATE AND FEDERAL FAIR HOUSING law, other antidiscrimination law, or meeting the housing needs of IMMIGRANT AND OTHER UNDERSERVED POPULATIONS.
Those two one-hour requirements DO NOT APPLY to licensees engaged SOLELY IN COMMERCIAL real estate who FILE A VERIFICATION of that status with the Commissioner.

MODULE TRAINING: every licensee must take EITHER 3.75 OR 7.5 HOURS of module training EVERY LICENCE YEAR within the 30 hours. The Commissioner determines the topics and credit hours each year, consulting a statewide trade association and a statewide private provider, and must publicise the outline NO LATER THAN APRIL 1 each year. Module credit depends on PASSING A WRITTEN TEST drawn from a Commissioner-approved question pool; the test may not be allocated more than ONE-SIXTH of the module's time.
A BROKER'S 30 hours must include a module of AT LEAST ONE HOUR EACH LICENCE YEAR specifically addressing issues relevant to BROKERS.
COURSES THAT GET NO CREDIT: MOTIVATION, SALESMANSHIP, PSYCHOLOGY OR TIME MANAGEMENT. The Commissioner MAY approve communication, marketing, negotiation and technology.

No credit for the SAME COURSE TWICE in one licensing period, as student or instructor. An approved 30-HOUR BROKER PRELICENSE COURSE MAY be used for continuing education credit if completed in the right period.

The Commissioner MAY NOT APPROVE a course that can be completed AT HOME OR OUTSIDE THE CLASSROOM WITHOUT INSTRUCTOR SUPERVISION, except accredited courses using NEW DELIVERY TECHNOLOGY, including interactive technology and the internet.

A broker MAY sponsor approved continuing education on the company's premises, but ALL OFFERINGS MUST BE OPEN TO ANY INTERESTED INDIVIDUAL - access may be restricted ONLY BY CLASS SIZE, and a course is NOT APPROVED if attendance is restricted to a particular group. The Commissioner SHALL NOT APPROVE PRELICENSE courses offered by, sponsored by or affiliated with any person or company licensed to engage in the real estate business.
Licensees MAY NOT CLAIM CREDIT for continuing education NOT ACTUALLY COMPLETED.

l: A renewed licence is VALID FOR 24 MONTHS, and a new licence issued during a 24-month period EXPIRES ON JUNE 30 of the expiration year assigned to it (82.63 subd. 5).

The BROKER renews the licence of each ELIGIBLE SALESPERSON - one who has demonstrated compliance with all renewal requirements BEFORE JUNE 15 of the renewal year. If the broker does not intend to renew an eligible salesperson, the broker must notify the salesperson IN WRITING 30 DAYS BEFORE JUNE 15. If the broker misses the deadline for an eligible salesperson, THE BROKER PAYS any resulting higher fees (82.62 subd. 2).

A person who has NOT RECEIVED NOTICE OF APPROVAL of renewal MAY NOT CONTINUE TO TRANSACT BUSINESS AFTER JUNE 30 of the renewal year until approval is received, and is UNLICENSED from JULY 1 until the licence is issued and received (82.62 subd. 3, subd. 4).
The Commissioner SHALL CANCEL the licence of a salesperson who fails to comply with the continuing education requirement (82.62 subd. 1).
NO EXAMINATION is required to renew - BUT a licensee who FAILS TO RENEW FOR TWO YEARS must TAKE THE EXAMINATION AGAIN (82.62 subd. 5).
If a licence lapses, the Commissioner may begin a revocation or suspension proceeding WITHIN TWO YEARS after the licence was last effective (82.62 subd. 6).
A SALESPERSON must be licensed to act ON BEHALF OF A LICENSED BROKER, and MAY NOT be licensed to act for MORE THAN ONE BROKER in this state at the same time (82.63 subd. 4).

When a salesperson TERMINATES activity on behalf of a broker, the salesperson's LICENCE IS INEFFECTIVE. The broker must NOTIFY THE COMMISSIONER WITHIN TEN DAYS. The salesperson may apply for TRANSFER to active status with another broker AT ANY TIME DURING THE REMAINDER OF THE LICENCE PERIOD; if not, a NEW LICENCE application is required (82.63 subd. 6).
The salesperson's licence IS NOT EFFECTIVE during any period in which the BROKER'S licence is SUSPENDED OR REVOKED; the salesperson may apply to transfer to another broker (82.82 subd. 2).
Each broker is RESPONSIBLE FOR THE ACTS of all the broker's salespeople and closing agents acting as agents on the broker's behalf (82.63 subd. 3).

A TEMPORARY BROKER'S PERMIT of 45 DAYS may be issued on the DEATH, INCAPACITY OR LOSS OF LICENCE of a broker, to someone with three years' salesperson experience who is otherwise reasonably qualified; it may be RENEWED ONCE on a showing of good-faith effort. Only salespersons licensed to the deceased or incapacitated broker at the time may conduct business under it (82.63 subd. 12).

An ADDITIONAL broker's licence requires a LEGITIMATE BUSINESS PURPOSE, capability to supervise (or no supervisory responsibility), and either AT LEAST 20 PERCENT OWNERSHIP in each business entity or officer/signing-partner/managing-member status in both entities (82.63 subd. 2).

TAX CLEARANCE: the Commissioner MAY NOT issue or renew a licence if the Commissioner of Revenue reports the applicant owes the state DELINQUENT TAXES OF $500 OR MORE, until a clearance certificate issues (82.82 subd. 9).

RECIPROCITY: the education and continuing education requirements may be waived where a WRITTEN RECIPROCAL AGREEMENT is in effect, the individual is LICENSED IN GOOD STANDING there, and that jurisdiction's requirements are SUBSTANTIALLY SIMILAR (82.64). PSI's bulletin notes a salesperson licensed in another state takes ONLY THE STATE PORTION.

sections.h: The Real Estate Education, Research and Recovery Fund (82.86)
l: The fund is ADMINISTERED BY THE COMMISSIONER OF COMMERCE; the COMMISSIONER OF MANAGEMENT AND BUDGET is its CUSTODIAN.

FEES: an INITIAL licensee pays $30; each renewing broker, salesperson and closing agent pays $20 PER LICENSING PERIOD in addition to the renewal fee. If the fund runs low the Commissioner may levy an ADDITIONAL ASSESSMENT NOT EXCEEDING $100 at renewal (82.86 subd. 3, subd. 4).

WHAT THE EDUCATION SIDE PAYS FOR: advancing education and research in real estate for licensees; underwriting educational seminars and projects; establishing a REAL ESTATE CHAIR OR COURSES at Minnesota state institutions of higher learning; contracting for research; the costs of defending actions against the fund, EXCLUDING ATTORNEY'S FEES; and providing PUBLIC INFORMATION ON HOUSING ISSUES including environmental safety and housing affordability (82.86 subd. 6).

RECOVERY: an aggrieved person who obtains a FINAL JUDGMENT against a licensee on grounds of FRAUDULENT, DECEPTIVE OR DISHONEST PRACTICES, or CONVERSION OF TRUST FUNDS, arising directly out of a transaction when the judgment debtor was licensed, may apply to the court that entered the judgment. A BANKRUPTCY DISCHARGE OF THE JUDGMENT DOES NOT BAR THE CLAIM.

THE CAPS: ACTUAL AND DIRECT OUT-OF-POCKET LOSS, EXCLUDING ATTORNEY'S FEES AND INTEREST, up to $150,000 PER CLAIMANT PER TRANSACTION regardless of the number of persons aggrieved or parcels involved, and NO MORE THAN $250,000 PER LICENSEE regardless of the number of claims. JOINT TENANTS AND TENANTS IN COMMON COUNT AS A SINGLE CLAIMANT.

WHO MAY NOT RECOVER: a GOVERNMENT AGENCY, a FINANCIAL INSTITUTION or other entity that purchases, guarantees or insures a loan secured by real estate; and a LICENSEE, except one acting AS PRINCIPAL buying or selling their own property. UNDER NO CIRCUMSTANCES may a licensee recover for the LOSS OF A COMMISSION OR SIMILAR FEE.

Recovery is limited to transactions where the property is intended for the buyer's DIRECT PERSONAL HABITATION OR COMMERCIAL USE, and is NOT AVAILABLE where the buyer's participation was FOR INVESTMENT PURPOSES ONLY, limited to providing capital.

AT THE HEARING the claimant must show, among other things, that they are NOT THE SPOUSE OF THE DEBTOR (or that spouse's personal representative), that they made ALL REASONABLE SEARCHES for the debtor's assets and took all necessary action to realise them, and that they DILIGENTLY PURSUED REMEDIES against all judgment debtors and others liable.

ACCELERATED PAYMENT: claims not exceeding the CONCILIATION COURT jurisdiction limit are paid on an accelerated basis - the Commissioner mails the licensee a copy of the application and pays at the END OF 15 DAYS unless the licensee reports an APPEAL, and PAYMENT AUTOMATICALLY SUSPENDS THE LICENSEE'S LICENCE. No more than $50,000 against one licensee may be paid under the accelerated process, prorated if claims exceed it.
The hearing on a court application is held 30 DAYS AFTER SERVICE on the Commissioner, continuable up to 60 further days on the Commissioner's petition.

mn/license.summary: Seven items. Minnesota's education comes in THREE 30-hour courses - one before the exam, two before the licence - and continuing education is 30 hours per 24-month period with a front-loaded deadline. Learn the recovery fund caps.
traps: Education is 30 hours BEFORE the exam and 60 more BEFORE the application - not 90 hours up front.
At least 15 of the 30 continuing education hours must land in the FIRST 12 MONTHS of the 24-month period.
Motivation, salesmanship, psychology and time management earn NO continuing education credit.
Fail to renew for TWO YEARS and the examination must be retaken.
The recovery fund is $150,000 per claimant per transaction and $250,000 per LICENSEE - and a licensee can never recover a lost commission.
Accelerated payment SUSPENDS the licensee's licence automatically.
75% is needed on EACH portion separately, not on the combined 130 items.
vocab: Course I, II and III
Minnesota's three 30-hour prelicense courses; Course I comes before the examination, Courses II and III before the licence application (82.59 subd. 8, 82.60).
Module training
The 3.75 or 7.5 hours of Commissioner-set topics each licence year, inside the 30 continuing education hours, credited only on passing a written test (82.61(h)).
Eligible salesperson
One who has met all renewal requirements before June 15 of the renewal year, whom the broker must then renew (82.62 subd. 2).
Real Estate Education, Research and Recovery Fund
The state fund that pays unsatisfied judgments for fraud or conversion of trust funds, up to $150,000 per claimant per transaction and $250,000 per licensee (82.86).
Temporary broker's permit
The 45-day permit, renewable once, issued on a broker's death, incapacity or loss of licence (82.63 subd. 12).
Limited broker's license
A licence authorising transactions as principal only, or negotiation of non-residential mortgage loans; no salesperson may be licensed under an individual limited broker (82.63 subd. 13).

mn/trust.blurb: Who holds the earnest money, deposit and disbursement deadlines, commingling, the interest.
examples: A buyer's broker takes a $5,000 check on Monday. The seller accepts on Thursday. The purchase agreement says nothing about timing.
The money belongs in the LISTING broker's trust account, and the three-business-day clock runs from the LATER event - final acceptance on Thursday - not from Monday's receipt (82.75 subd. 5(b), (c)).
The deal dies and the parties each demand the deposit.

The broker holds the money. Disbursement needs a closing, a written agreement of the parties, a 559.217 affidavit, or a court order. The broker does not choose a winner - and where the SELLER could not close through no fault of the buyer, the broker may not claim any of it absent a separate agreement with the buyer (82.75 subd. 5(d), 82.81 subd. 3).

sections.h: Whose account, and when it goes in (82.75 subd. 1, 5)
l: ALL TRUST FUNDS received by a broker, the broker's salespeople or closing agents must be DEPOSITED IN A TRUST ACCOUNT maintained by the broker for that purpose in a BANK, SAVINGS ASSOCIATION, CREDIT UNION OR INDUSTRIAL LOAN AND THRIFT COMPANY with deposit liabilities - EXCEPT as the money may be paid to one of the parties under an EXPRESS WRITTEN AGREEMENT between the parties.
The depository must be a MINNESOTA BANK OR TRUST COMPANY, or any FOREIGN BANK that AUTHORISES THE COMMISSIONER TO EXAMINE its records of the deposits on demand.
UNLESS THE PARTIES AGREE OTHERWISE IN WRITING, THE BROKER WITH WHOM TRUST FUNDS ARE DEPOSITED IS THE LISTING BROKER (82.75 subd. 5(b)).

Earnest money from a potential buyer goes into the LISTING BROKER'S trust account PURSUANT TO THE TERMS OF THE WRITTEN AGREEMENT between the parties. IF THE AGREEMENT IS SILENT about timing, the listing broker must deposit it WITHIN THREE BUSINESS DAYS of EITHER RECEIPT OF THE EARNEST MONEY OR FINAL ACCEPTANCE OF THE PURCHASE AGREEMENT, WHICHEVER IS LATER (82.75 subd. 5(c)).
IF THE OFFER IS REJECTED, the earnest money must be returned to the potential buyer NOT LATER THAN THE NEXT BUSINESS DAY after rejection (82.75 subd. 5(c)).
FAILING TO MAINTAIN A TRUST ACCOUNT AT ALL TIMES, as the law provides, is a fraudulent, deceptive or dishonest practice (82.81 subd. 12(a)(15)).

sections.h: Getting it out, and keeping it clean (82.75 subd. 3, 4, 5, 9, 10)
l: Trust funds must STAY in the trust account UNTIL DISBURSEMENT UNDER THIS SECTION AND PROPER ACCOUNTING to the parties entitled to it.

TRUST FUNDS MAY ONLY BE DISBURSED ON ONE OF FOUR EVENTS: a CLOSING of the transaction; WRITTEN AGREEMENT BETWEEN THE PARTIES; PURSUANT TO AN AFFIDAVIT required under section 559.217; or A COURT ORDER (82.75 subd. 5(d)).
DISBURSEMENT MUST BE MADE WITHIN TEN BUSINESS DAYS following the CONSUMMATION OR TERMINATION of a transaction IF THE AGREEMENTS ARE SILENT as to the time of disbursement (82.75 subd. 5(d)).

COMMINGLING: only trust funds may be deposited in a trust account, and a broker, salesperson or closing agent may NOT COMMINGLE personal or other funds - EXCEPT a SPECIFICALLY IDENTIFIED SUM OF PERSONAL FUNDS used to PAY SERVICE CHARGES OR SATISFY THE MINIMUM BALANCE requirement (82.75 subd. 4). Commingling is also a fraudulent, deceptive or dishonest practice (82.81 subd. 12(a)(12)).

NONDEPOSITABLE ITEMS - a NOTE, BOND, STOCK CERTIFICATE, TREASURY BILL or other instrument or thing of value taken IN LIEU OF CASH - must be DEPOSITED IMMEDIATELY WITH AN AUTHORISED ESCROW AGENT whose authority rests on a WRITTEN AGREEMENT EXECUTED BY THE OFFEROR AND THE ESCROW AGENT, and a RECEIPT must be issued to the buyer for its value. If the BROKER acts as escrow agent, the broker needs WRITTEN AUTHORITY FROM BUYER AND SELLER, the parties must be told the item's NATURE, AMOUNT AND CUSTODIAN, and the holding must be RECORDED IN THE TRUST ACCOUNT RECORDS (82.75 subd. 3).

SPECIAL ACCOUNTS: trust funds may go into an INTEREST-BEARING ACCOUNT OR CERTIFICATE OF DEPOSIT only if BUYER AND SELLER CONSENT IN WRITING to the account AND to the disposition of the funds INCLUDING ANY INTEREST (82.75 subd. 9).

LICENSEE AS PRINCIPAL: funds that WOULD BE trust funds if received by an agent must, if received by a LICENSEE ACTING AS PRINCIPAL, go into a TRUST ACCOUNT, unless a written agreement SIGNED BY ALL PARTIES specifies a different disposition - and that agreement must STATE that the funds would otherwise be placed in a real estate trust account (82.75 subd. 10). Receiving such funds without doing so is a fraudulent, deceptive or dishonest practice (82.81 subd. 12(a)(3)).

A licensee acting as principal where the SELLER RETAINS ANY LIABILITY for an obligation on the property must deposit in a trust account the parts of all contract payments needed to meet amounts CONCURRENTLY DUE on existing mortgages, contracts for deed or other instruments, plus RESERVES FOR TAXES AND INSURANCE, and must hold them until disbursement under the encumbrance's terms (82.75 subd. 2).

l: EACH BROKER MUST MAINTAIN A POOLED INTEREST-BEARING TRUST ACCOUNT for client funds. The INTEREST, LESS REASONABLE TRANSACTION COSTS, MUST BE PAID TO THE MINNESOTA HOUSING FINANCE AGENCY for deposit in the HOUSING TRUST FUND ACCOUNT under section 462A.201 - UNLESS the parties to a transaction specify otherwise by EXPRESS WRITTEN AGREEMENT (82.75 subd. 8(a)).

The broker must DIRECT THE FINANCIAL INSTITUTION to pay that interest AT LEAST QUARTERLY to the Agency and to SEND A STATEMENT showing the broker's name, the interest rate applied, the service charges deducted and the account balance for the period. The institution must PROMPTLY NOTIFY THE AGENCY IF A DRAFT IS DISHONORED (82.75 subd. 8).

NOTICE OF TRUST ACCOUNT STATUS: the names of the institutions and the TRUST ACCOUNT NUMBERS must be given to the Commissioner AT THE TIME OF APPLICATION for the licence. The broker must IMMEDIATELY REPORT ANY CHANGE of trust account status - institutions, account numbers or additional accounts. A broker or closing agent MAY NOT CLOSE AN EXISTING TRUST ACCOUNT WITHOUT GIVING TEN DAYS' WRITTEN NOTICE TO THE COMMISSIONER (82.75 subd. 6).

RECORDS OF ALL TRUST FUNDS RECEIVED, including notes, savings certificates and UNCASHED OR UNCOLLECTED CHECKS, must show the DATE FUNDS WERE RECEIVED, FROM WHOM, THE AMOUNT, the DATE OF DEPOSIT, the CHECK NUMBER OR DATE of related disbursements, and A MONTHLY BALANCE of the trust account.

Each broker must keep a FORMAL TRUST CASH RECEIPTS JOURNAL and a FORMAL CASH DISBURSEMENT JOURNAL, or similar records, IN ACCORDANCE WITH GENERALLY ACCEPTED ACCOUNTING PRINCIPLES. All records and funds are SUBJECT TO INSPECTION BY THE COMMISSIONER OR AN AGENT AT ANY TIME.

A SEPARATE RECORD FOR EACH BENEFICIARY OR TRANSACTION must identify the transaction and the parties and show the DATE AND AMOUNT DEPOSITED and, for each related disbursement, its DATE, CHECK NUMBER, AMOUNT AND DESCRIPTION (82.75 subd. 11).

A broker's review of ALL TRUST ACCOUNT BOOKS AND RECORDS is part of the broker's SUPERVISION duty (82.73 subd. 3(a)), and trust account records are among the documents RETAINED SIX YEARS (82.72 subd. 3).

RESIDENTIAL SECURITY DEPOSITS are not trust funds of this kind: a landlord holds them for the tenant and they bear SIMPLE NONCOMPOUNDED INTEREST AT ONE PERCENT PER ANNUM, with any interest amount UNDER $1 EXCLUDED (504B.178 subd. 2). A broker may maintain interest-bearing accounts for such deposits under 504B.178 (82.75 subd. 7).

mn/trust.summary: Four items, and they turn on three numbers: the LISTING broker holds the money by default, deposit within THREE BUSINESS DAYS of receipt or final acceptance whichever is LATER, and disburse within TEN BUSINESS DAYS of consummation or termination when the paperwork is silent.
traps: The LISTING broker holds the earnest money by default - not the buyer's broker.
Three business days of receipt OR FINAL ACCEPTANCE, WHICHEVER IS LATER. Candidates drop the 'whichever is later'.
A REJECTED offer's earnest money goes back by the NEXT BUSINESS DAY.
Ten BUSINESS days to disburse after consummation or termination, when the paperwork is silent.
Only four disbursement triggers: closing, written agreement, a 559.217 affidavit, or a court order. A broker never decides a dispute alone.
Pooled trust interest goes to the MINNESOTA HOUSING FINANCE AGENCY, not the broker and not the buyer.
Ten days' WRITTEN notice to the Commissioner before closing a trust account.
vocab: Trust funds
Money received by a broker, salesperson or closing agent belonging to another in a real estate transaction, which must reach a dedicated trust account (82.75).
Nondepositable item
A note, bond, stock certificate, treasury bill or similar thing of value taken in lieu of cash, which goes immediately to an authorised escrow agent (82.75 subd. 3).
Pooled interest-bearing trust account
The account every broker must maintain, whose interest less costs goes to the Minnesota Housing Finance Agency's housing trust fund (82.75 subd. 8).
559.217 affidavit
The statutory affidavit procedure for cancelling a purchase agreement, and one of the four events permitting disbursement of trust funds (82.75 subd. 5(d)).
Commingling
Mixing personal or other funds with trust funds, permitted only as an identified sum for service charges or the minimum balance (82.75 subd. 4).
